investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes expose the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource but reported it as exhausted (Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm); the other four nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the two eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on the affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained unscheduled for 132–148 seconds across all three checks before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence output and a full contract-gap failure.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing remote-agent pods or other workloads, leaving no capacity for new scheduling requests. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not carry the required label or taint that the remote-agent pod spec targets, reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes and amplifying the impact of any capacity shortfall.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the total kata.peerpods.io/vm quota across the 2 eligible nodes is too small to absorb concurrent eval runs (all three sibling checks attempted pod creation within a ~7-minute window, each failing with the same exhaustion message).

Lower probability — pod spec node affinity/selector recently tightened or changed, shrinking the eligible node set from more than 2 to exactly 2 nodes, which would make the cluster more sensitive to VM slot exhaustion.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing — Kubernetes Cluster Exhausted of kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-06-20 with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: the 6-node cluster has zero available kata.peerpods.io/vm slots (only 2 nodes carry the resource and both are exhausted) and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the eval's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1905) could not schedule a VM-backed pod, no agent was ever created, and the check returned zero evidence — leaving all four required fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) missing from the contract output.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent runtime has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota across the two eligible nodes. When the eval runner calls createAgent with type "remote" (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1905), the scheduler cannot place the pod: 2 nodes report "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" and 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. The pod remains Unschedulable for ~132–152 seconds across all three checks before the eval times out. Because no pod is ever scheduled, no agent identity or state is produced, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-state (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) is entirely unmet. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the kata/peer-pods VM resource pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never left the pending state, meaning the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes expose the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource but reported it as exhausted (Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm); the other four nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable: no lower-priority victims existed on the two eligible nodes, and preemption cannot help on the affinity-mismatched nodes. The pod remained unscheduled for 132–148 seconds across all three checks before the eval timed out, producing zero evidence output and a full contract-gap failure.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are occupied by existing remote-agent pods or other workloads, leaving no capacity for new scheduling requests. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not carry the required label or taint that the remote-agent pod spec targets, reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes and amplifying the impact of any capacity shortfall.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the total kata.peerpods.io/vm quota across the 2 eligible nodes is too small to absorb concurrent eval runs (all three sibling checks attempted pod creation within a ~7-minute window, each failing with the same exhaustion message).

Lower probability — pod spec node affinity/selector recently tightened or changed, shrinking the eligible node set from more than 2 to exactly 2 nodes, which would make the cluster more sensitive to VM slot exhaustion.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe on the two kata-capable nodes shows available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity (i.e., Allocatable > Requests), the exhaustion hypothesis would be disproved and the cause would shift to a scheduler bug or misconfiguration.

If the remote-agent-state eval passes on a re-run without any infrastructure change, the failure was transient (e.g., a burst of concurrent pods that have since terminated) rather than a sustained capacity ceiling.
If the pod spec's node affinity/selector is found to be misconfigured to exclude all 6 nodes (not just 4), the root cause would be a configuration error rather than resource exhaustion.

If a non-remote-agents workload is found to be consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the two eligible nodes, the root cause would be resource contention from an unrelated service rather than remote-agent demand alone.

If the cluster is found to have more than 6 nodes with kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity that are simply not visible to the scheduler (e.g., NotReady), the root cause would be node health rather than capacity exhaustion.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check that directly queries the kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity across all cluster nodes and alerts when available slots fall below a configurable threshold, providing earlier warning before pod scheduling fails.

Add a pre-flight eval check that verifies at least one node with kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity is schedulable before attempting remote-agent creation, so scheduling failures are diagnosed at the infrastructure layer rather than surfaced as missing evidence in the agent-state contract.
Add a leaked-pod detection eval that enumerates remote-agent pods older than a configurable TTL and flags them, preventing VM slot exhaustion from accumulated zombie pods.

Consider adding a historical baseline to the remote-agent-state check (currently previousRunCount=0, lastPassingAt=null) so that regressions from a known-passing state can be detected and alerted on automatically.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place agent pods: 2 of 6 nodes report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence was collected by any check, confirming the agent VM was never provisioned and the runtime response contract was never reached.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that carry it, and the other 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption candidates available, every remote-agent pod request times out unscheduled before the agent can be created, reach a ready state, or serve a runtime response. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents VM pool in the production-api environment; it is an eval failure reflecting a real infrastructure constraint, but no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a broader user-facing outage.

possibleCauses: kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource pool is fully consumed on the 2 eligible nodes — no VM slots remain for new agent pods, and no existing pods are preemptible (scheduler message: 'No preemption victims found').

Node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod spec restricts scheduling to a specific node label or taint that only 2 of 6 nodes satisfy, and those 2 nodes are already at VM capacity — a misconfigured or overly narrow affinity would produce exactly this split (2 Insufficient resource, 4 affinity mismatch).
The kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota or limit range for the namespace has been set too low relative to concurrent eval or workload demand, causing resource exhaustion under normal load.
A prior eval run or workload left orphaned remote-agent pods that are holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without being cleaned up, reducing available capacity for new scheduling attempts.

recommendedNextActions: Immediately inspect the Kubernetes cluster for kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion: check node capacity, allocatable counts, and currently consuming pods across all 6 nodes.
Identify and clean up any orphaned or stuck remote-agent pods that are holding kata.peerpods.io/vm slots without serving active workloads.
Review the node affinity and node selector on the remote-agent pod spec to determine whether the restriction to 2 eligible nodes is intentional; if not, evaluate expanding the eligible node pool.
If VM slot exhaustion is confirmed as a persistent capacity issue, evaluate increasing the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota or adding additional eligible nodes to the pool.
Re-run the three remote-agents eval checks after any remediation to confirm recovery before closing the investigation.

Because remote-agent-create and remote-agent-state are required=true and the feature is configured degradedAfterFailures=1 / outageAfterFailures=2, verify the feature's current health status in the observability dashboard and determine whether an incident should be declared based on internal policy.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If the Kubernetes cluster shows available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity on the eligible nodes at the time of the eval run, the scheduling exhaustion hypothesis would be weakened and an alternative cause (e.g., API-level rejection, auth failure, or network partition) would need to be investigated.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after this failure succeeds and collects all required evidence, it would suggest the exhaustion was transient (e.g., a concurrent workload released VM slots) rather than a persistent capacity problem.

If the pod spec's node affinity or selector is intentionally narrow and the 2 eligible nodes have remaining kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, the root cause would shift to a different scheduling constraint not visible in the current evidence.
If orphaned pods are found and cleaned up and the eval then passes, it would confirm the orphan-holding-slots hypothesis over a hard capacity limit.
If the eval runner logs show the probe returned before the scheduling timeout due to an API error (rather than a scheduler Unschedulable event), the root cause would be upstream of the scheduler.
followUpEvals: Add an eval that directly probes kata.peerpods.io/vm node capacity and reports available vs. allocated VM slots as evidence fields, enabling early warning before scheduling exhaustion causes agent pod failures.

Add an eval that detects orphaned remote-agent pods (pods in non-terminal states older than a configurable threshold) and reports their count and ages as evidence, catching resource-holding leaks before they exhaust the pool.

Add a scheduling-latency eval that measures time-to-scheduled for a remote-agent pod and fails at a lower threshold than the current 148s unscheduled timeout, providing earlier signal of capacity pressure.

Consider adding a synthetic eval that verifies at least one kata.peerpods.io/vm slot is available on an eligible node before attempting full agent creation, allowing the scheduling-layer failure to be distinguished from agent-runtime failures in future reports.
